answer.location_description: Small 3x3 square near the top-left corner of the image, rows 1-3, columns 1-3.
answer.mechanism: Several layer-1 units have very large weights confined to the 3x3 top-left patch, far stronger than their weights elsewhere. Units 1, 7, 11, 12, 14, 16 and 19 have large positive patch weights (about +55 to +99), and these same units mostly also respond to a bright ring at large radius, so they are large-blob detectors. Units 3, 5, 8, 10, 17, 20, 23, 25, 30 and 31 have large negative patch weights (about -30 to -99), and these are the small-blob or background detectors with negative rings. In layer 2, units u13, u8 and u15, which have positive output weights (+99, +65, +67), take strong positive input from the patch-positive units and strong negative input from the patch-negative units. Units u3, u9 and u12, which have negative output weights (-94, -98, -72), take the opposite pattern. A bright patch therefore turns on the class-1 pathway and suppresses the class-0 pathway, pushing the logit positive.
answer.evidence: Patch weights by unit, rows 1-3 and cols 1-3. Positive: unit 1 = 66,59,98 / 59,96,71 / 70,88,66; unit 11 = 94,82,76 / ...; unit 12 = 76,55,86 / 98,95,62 / 83,81,97; unit 16 = 83,99,97 / ... Negative: unit 3 = -91,-78,-84 / ...; unit 5 = -84,-74,-95 / ...; unit 31 = -92,-67,-89 / .... Surrounding pixels such as column 0, row 0 and row 4 have ordinary small weights. Layer-2 inputs: u13 gets h7 +87, h19 +78, h14 +68 and h17 -92, h25 -87, h5 -78. u8 gets h14 +99, h11 +95 and h8 -97, h3 -86. u3 gets h14 -93, h16 -81 and h17 +87, h25 +87. Output weights: u13 +99, u8 +65, u15 +67, u3 -94, u9 -98.
answer.main_feature: Genuine size cue: units respond to how far the bright region extends from the centre. A positive ring of weights at radius about 4-7 pixels, rows 6-17, signals a large blob, while units with a negative ring and positive background signal a small blob.
